Article Title: J&K CM Omar Abdullah announces Rs 10 lakh aid after Kulgam terror attack kills two labourers
Article Text:
The attack took place late on Friday evening in the Kelam area of south Kashmir, where unidentified gunmen opened fire on the workers

NEW DELHI: Jammu and Kashmir chief minister Omar Abdullah on Saturday announced an ex gratia payment of Rs 10 lakh each for the families of two migrant labourers from Chhattisgarh who were killed in a terrorist attack at a brick kiln in Kulgam district.The attack took place late on Friday evening in the Kelam area of south Kashmir, where unidentified gunmen opened fire on the workers. The victims, both in their 20s, had travelled to the Valley in search of work after leaving their villages in Chhattisgarh.One of the labourers, 24-year-old Deepak Ratre, died before he could be taken to hospital. The second victim, 28-year-old Bhupendra Bhaina, was initially admitted to Government Medical College, Anantnag, before being shifted to SKIMS Hospital in Srinagar, where he later succumbed to his injuries.Deepak, from Bundeli village in Sakti district, was the sole breadwinner for his family, which includes his elderly mother, a physically disabled younger brother, his wife and their four-month-old son. His uncle said Deepak had moved to Jammu and Kashmir around seven to eight months ago with his wife to work at the brick kiln in the hope of building a better future.Bhupendra, from Chhuiya village in Sarangarh-Bilaigarh district, had reached Kashmir around three months ago with his wife.The couple had left their four-year-old son in the care of his grandmother and younger sister while other family members worked as labourers in Himachal Pradesh.Chhattisgarh chief minister Vishnu Deo Sai expressed grief over the killings, describing the attack as "cowardly". He said the state government stood firmly with the bereaved families and had directed officials to coordinate with the Jammu and Kashmir administration to bring the bodies back home.
Article Summary: The attack took place late on Friday evening in the Kelam area of south Kashmir. The victims, both in their 20s, had travelled to the Valley in search of work. One of the labourers, 24-year-old Deepak Ratre, died before he could be taken to hospital.

Article Title: 'Forgiveness only on reel or will you withdraw cases?': Abhijeet Dipke comments on PM Modi's late night video
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi 's call for compassion towards students accused of abusing him at the Jantar Mantar protest has triggered a fresh response, with Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke questioning whether the message of forgiveness would extend beyond words.Reacting to the Prime Minister's selfie-style Instagram video, Dipke wrote, "Fraand, sirf reel par hi maaf karoge ya cases bhi wapas loge?(Friend, will you forgive them only through reels, or will you also withdraw the cases?)"The Prime Minister's video, shared on his official Instagram and X handles on Friday, came after a 15-year old protester from Noida was booked for allegedly using derogatory language against him during at Delhi's Jantar Mantar.In the video, PM Modi said, "Today I just feel like talking to you. The country and the world have witnessed what happened at Jantar Mantar. Some mischievous children used very crude and abusive language, words that do not befit any civilized society. I was personally abused, and even my late mother was subjected to abuse. It was a truly ugly spectacle."Acknowledging the public outrage over the incident, the Prime Minister urged people to view the matter through the lens of reform rather than punishment.He said that while the students' remarks had understandably outraged society, mistakes are part of growing up. He urged people to forgive them, guide them in the right direction, and help them reform, saying the students had "lost their way" but deserved an opportunity to correct themselves.The Prime Minister further argued against prolonged legal action and social ostracisation."Punishing them, dragging them through court proceedings, and harassing them in society, none of this will change the situation. I want to forgive them. Society, too, should accept this," PM Modi said, while urging the students to learn from their mistakes and move forward.Earlier, Dipke had questioned the police action and alleged selective enforcement of the law.In a video shared by CJP on X, he said, "If you are registering cases for abusing, when will cases be registered against those BJP IT Cell people who have been using abusive language for women online for years?"He further alleged that several social media users identifying themselves with the BJP had routinely targeted women online."They have been using all kinds of words, not respecting women from any angle. And they proudly wrote in their bio, 'Followed by PM Modi'. Such people have abused girls. When will the case be filed on them?" Dipke said.Questioning the criminal proceedings, Dipke argued that abusive language, while objectionable, should not automatically attract criminal prosecution."If cases are to be filed for abusing, highest number of cases will be filed against the BJP's IT Cell, because they are the ones who have abused women the most. And it will be against BJP's leaders, who have used bad language for years, even inside the Parliament," he said.In a post accompanying the video, CJP asked, "Will an FIR be filed against all those IT Cell members who have been abusing women for the last several years?"This is not the first time Dipke has publicly reacted to one of the Prime Minister's social media videos. Earlier on Thursday, after PM Modi released a video message highlighting the recently passed anti-paper leak legislation, Dipke commented on Instagram, "Your skin is brighter than the country's future."The Prime Minister had described the legislation as a key reform aimed at strengthening the examination system.
Article Summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi has called for compassion towards students accused of abusing him at the Jantar Mantar protest. Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke questioned whether the message of forgiveness would extend beyond words. Dipke had questioned the police action and alleged selective enforcement of the law.

Article Title: First J&K terror attack on migrants in 21 months: Two Chhattisgarh labourers die after being shot
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: The death toll in Friday night's terror attack on migrant labourers in Jammu and Kashmir's Kulgam rose to two on Saturday after a Chhattisgarh worker succumbed to injuries in hospital, officials told news agency PTI.The attack took place late Friday night in the Kelam area of south Kashmir, where the two workers were employed at a brick kiln. Officials said both men sustained critical injuries after terrorists fired at them.One of the labourers, identified as Deepak Ratray, died before he could be shifted to a hospital. The second victim, Bopinder, was initially admitted to Government Medical College (GMC) Anantnag before being referred to SKIMS Hospital in Soura, where he later succumbed to his injuries.Officials said both victims were in their twenties and had travelled from Chhattisgarh in search of work.The incident comes days after terrorists shot dead Jammu and Kashmir Police head constable Ashiq Hussain Qureshi at Anantnag's Lal Chowk while he was deployed on Amarnath Yatra duty. That attack, on July 22, was the first terror strike in Kashmir since the April 22, 2025 Pahalgam massacre, in which 26 people were killed.Friday's attack has also revived concerns over the safety of migrant workers in the Valley. In February 2024, two non-local labourers from Punjab, Amritpal Singh and Rohit Masih, were shot dead in Srinagar. Before that, in October 2021, terrorists killed two workers from Bihar, Raja Reshi Dev and Joginder Reshi Dev, in Kulgam's Wanpoh area.Lieutenant governor Manoj Sinha condemned the latest attack and said security forces had been instructed to intensify anti-terror operations."I strongly condemn this cowardly act. I have directed our security forces to step up their operations and eliminate the terrorists," Sinha wrote on X, adding that he had spoken to DGP Nalin Prabhat and other senior security officials.PDP president and former chief minister Mehbooba Mufti also condemned the killings."They work themselves to the bone far away from home only to feed their families. Unimaginably cruel to target them in such senseless acts of violence," she said.BJP's Jammu and Kashmir spokesperson Altaf Thakur described the attack as "cowardly, barbaric and inhuman", alleging that its objective was to disturb peace and normalcy in the Union Territory.The attack occurred during the ongoing Amarnath Yatra, which began on July 3. While the pilgrimage through the Pahalgam route has remained suspended since July 19 because of heavy rain and landslides, the Baltal route in Ganderbal continues to remain operational.Following the attack, security forces launched a cordon-and-search operation in the area to trace those responsible.
Article Summary: The attack took place late Friday night in the Kelam area of south Kashmir. One of the labourers, identified as Deepak Ratray, died before he could be shifted to a hospital. The second victim, Bopinder, was initially admitted to Government Medical College before being referred to SKIMS Hospital in Soura.

Article Title: SC: How is torching a police station UAPA offence?
Article Text:
Dismisses Plea Against Bail To ‘Mastermind’

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Implementing its view that bail granted by a HC should not be ordinarily challenged in the apex court, Supreme Court Friday dismissed Uttarakhand's appeal questioning the grant of bail to one Abdul Malik , the alleged mastermind of a mob that hurled a petrol bomb to torch a police station in Haldwani in 2024.A bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana asked whether throwing a bomb constitutes an offence under UPA. "Is throwing a bomb a UAPA offence?" the bench asked the state additional advocate general Gaurav Bhatia before he could open arguments for cancellation of bail granted to Malik by HC."If a mob burns a police station, how is it an offence under UAPA? How did the offence affect national security? We have doubts about invocation of UAPA charges against the accused, that is why we are not inclined to entertain the appeal," Justice Bagchi said.Bhatia tried to impress upon the court the seriousness of the offence. "The accused is the mastermind behind mobilising the mob and one of his key associates threw petrol bombs to burn the police station, which is an offence that attracts a life sentence. Just because some co-accused got bail, he should not be granted the same relief without appreciating the gravity of the crime committed by him," he said.When the AAG said the HC passed a cursory order granting bail without giving reasons, the CJI said, "In light of the facts of the case, there was no need for a detailed order.SC has ruled repeatedly that bail should not be granted mechanically. Here the judge has applied his mind before granting bail."Bhatia said if a person who engineers such violence gets bail then it would have a demoralising effect on the police force. The bench disagreed and said, "If that is the concern of the state, then its prosecution should have ensured speedy trial and provided cogent evidence to secure conviction of the accused."The apex court bench dismissed the appeal but clarified that it has expressed no opinion on the merits of the case.
Article Summary: Supreme Court dismisses Uttarakhand's appeal questioning the grant of bail to one Abdul Malik. Malik is alleged mastermind of a mob that hurled a petrol bomb to torch a police station in Haldwani in 2024. A bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana asked whether throwing a bomb constitutes an offence under UPA.

Article Title: 'Pak-trained Mujahideen have turned their guns inwards': India slams Islamabad over PoK crackdown
Article Text:
The MEA criticized Pakistan's harsh crackdown on protesters in Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir. (PTI images)

NEW DELHI: India on Friday slammed Pakistan of making an open admission of state-sponsored terrorism after a senior aide to Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif acknowledged that Islamabad had trained and armed Mujahideen who have now turned against the Pakistani state.The ministry of external affairs (MEA) also condemned Pakistan's crackdown on anti-government protesters in Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir (PoJK), alleging that more than 40 civilians had been killed.Addressing the weekly media briefing, MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said Pakistan's handling of the protests had exposed its treatment of civilians in the region."As you and all of us have witnessed, the Pakistani establishment continues to unleash ruthless force against peaceful civilians in Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir. This crackdown has resulted in the tragic death of over 40 innocent people, and many more have been seriously injured. It's the establishment's absolute disdain for the innocent people of Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir that was laid bare when their Defence Minister branded the protesting civilians as enemies," Jaiswal said.Referring to recent remarks by Pakistan Prime Minister's Special Assistant on Political Affairs Rana Sanaullah, Jaiswal said the statement amounted to a public acknowledgement that Pakistan had trained, funded and armed militants who were later sent into India."The Special Assistant of the Prime Minister [of Pakistan] on Political Affairs has openly admitted that the very Mujahideen that the Pakistani establishment trained, funded, armed, and sent to India have turned their guns inwards, weaponising themselves against the state," Jaiswal said.The remarks came after Sanaullah, in an interview with Geo News, said: "are the same people we once trained as Mujahideen. We sent them to fight, and today they are hanging around our necks."India has long accused Pakistan of sponsoring cross-border terrorism, an allegation Islamabad has consistently denied.Jaiswal also criticised the recently held elections in Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir, calling them a rejection of Pakistan's establishment."The so-called elections stand as a humiliating rejection of the Pakistan establishment. Facing a violent regime, the people have requested international organisations for an independent investigation into the unlawful killings. We urged that the international community should scrutinise Pakistan's actions and hold it accountable for its atrocities," Jaiswal said.According to ANI, widespread protests have erupted across PoJK over allegations of electoral rigging, political interference and suppression of democratic rights.The United Kashmir People's National Party (UKPNP) has appealed to the United Nations and the international community to intervene over what it described as a worsening human rights situation in the region.In a statement posted on X, the organisation urged international institutions, governments and human rights organisations to take immediate steps to protect civilians, ensure accountability and uphold international human rights law.The group specifically appealed to the United Nations, the European Union, the United Kingdom, the United States, Canada, Germany, France, Italy, Switzerland, Sweden, Norway, Russia and China, as well as international human rights organisations and global media, to respond to the reported escalation of violence in Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir.India has consistently maintained that Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir is an integral part of India and has repeatedly raised concerns over Pakistan's support for cross-border terrorism and its treatment of civilians in the region.
Article Summary: The ministry of external affairs (MEA) also condemned Pakistan's crackdown on anti-government protesters in Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir. MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said Pakistan's handling of the protests had exposed its treatment of civilians in the region.

Article Title: SC gives Rs 15L to kin of man killed by stray bull
Article Text: NEW DELHI: Setting a benchmark for compensation in cases of human death caused by stray cattle, particularly at a time when such incidents are on the rise across the country, SC, in a first-of-its-kind case, awarded Rs 15 lakh in compensation to the family of a man who died in 2007 when a bull attacked him in Punjab.Indicating that the state govt could not abdicate its responsibility towards people who get injured or die because of stray cattle, a bench of Justices Sanjay Karol and N K Singh directed all states to frame rules "to develop a mechanism for payment of compensation in accidents caused as a result of bovine/cattle, in both categories of cases, i.e. pedestrian or vehicular". It also asked govt to take care of strays and take action against owners who leave their animals on the streets and highways.

Article Title: 'Muslims can't regard country as deity': Islamic body objects to Vande Mataram Bill
Article Text:
The Board’s spokesperson, Dr SQR Ilyas, said that making Vande Mataram legally mandatory for all communities was incompatible with both constitutional principles and Islamic belief.

NEW DELHI: The All India Muslim Personal Law Board (AIMPLB) on Friday strongly criticised Parliament’s passage of a Bill that makes alleged disrespect to Vande Mataram a punishable offence, calling it an attack on religious and constitutional freedoms and urging the government not to impose patriotic expressions through legal compulsion.In a press release issued on 31 July, the Muslim body said the legislation was contrary to the constitutional, secular and democratic ethos of the country and amounted to a serious assault on the religious freedom of citizens. It argued that compelling participation in a song or slogan carrying religious connotations violated fundamental rights guaranteed under the Constitution.The Board’s spokesperson, Dr SQR Ilyas, said that making Vande Mataram legally mandatory for all communities was incompatible with both constitutional principles and Islamic belief.“Any attempt to make Vande Mataram compulsory for all sections and religious communities through legal coercion is not only objectionable but also contrary to the fundamental principles of the Constitution,” he said.The AIMPLB said that during the framing of the Constitution, the Constituent Assembly accepted only the first two stanzas of Vande Mataram at the national level, while the religious connotations of the remaining portions were not considered compatible with India’s secular character.Dr Ilyas argued that certain passages of the song depict the motherland in the form of a goddess and exhort people to worship her, which he said was contrary to the Islamic doctrine of Tawheed, or the absolute Oneness of God.“Therefore, compelling a Muslim to participate in a song, slogan or practice carrying a religious meaning contrary to his or her faith is wholly unacceptable,” he said.The Board also cited Articles 25 and 19 of the Constitution, saying they protect the freedom of religion and freedom of expression, including the right not to participate in expressions that conflict with an individual’s conscience.“These constitutional safeguards clearly imply that no citizen can be compelled to adopt or participate in any song, slogan, ideology or symbol against his or her religious beliefs and conscience,” the statement said.Referring to the Supreme Court’s landmark judgment in Bijoe Emmanuel v. State of Kerala, Dr Ilyas said the court had upheld this principle even in the context of the national anthem.“The Court held that a person could not be punished merely for not participating in an act when doing so was contrary to his or her religious beliefs. The Court also made it clear that, in certain circumstances, freedom of expression includes the right to remain silent, and that respectful non-participation cannot be regarded as disrespect.”The AIMPLB sought to distinguish between patriotism and religious devotion, saying that love for one’s country should not be equated with worship.“Love for the motherland and worship of the motherland are two entirely different concepts. Muslims deeply love their country and consider love for the homeland part of their civic and moral responsibility, but they cannot regard the country as a deity or goddess.”The Board added that patriotism should be judged by a citizen’s commitment to the Constitution, the country’s people and their rights rather than by the recitation of a particular slogan or song.It also urged the government to prioritise issues such as unemployment, inflation, poverty, education, healthcare, economic inequality and social injustice instead of pursuing what it described as sensitive and divisive measures.“Diverting public attention from fundamental issues by inflaming emotional and religious controversies serves neither the national interest nor the cause of democracy.”Concluding its statement, the AIMPLB said that India’s unity could only be strengthened by protecting constitutional supremacy, religious freedom and equal rights for all citizens.“A strong and united India can only be built where every citizen enjoys equal dignity, justice and freedom; where anyone’s patriotism is not judged through the prism of his or her religious beliefs; and where the supremacy of the Constitution, religious freedom and fundamental civil rights are protected at all costs.”The Vande Matram Bill, passed by both Houses of Parliament on Friday, seeks to make alleged disrespect to Vande Mataram a punishable offence and gives legal backing to its mandatory observance in specified contexts. Supporters have described the measure as a way to promote national unity and respect for a national symbol, while critics argue that it could compel citizens to participate in patriotic expressions regardless of their religious beliefs or freedom of conscience, raising concerns over constitutional rights and religious freedom.
Article Summary: The All India Muslim Personal Law Board (AIMPLB) has strongly criticised Parliament’s passage of a Bill that makes alleged disrespect to Vande Mataram a punishable offence. The Board said the legislation was contrary to the constitutional, secular and democratic ethos of the country. It argued that compelling participation in a song or slogan carrying religious connotations violated fundamental rights.

Article Title: Delhi riots 2020: Why Tahir Hussain escaped death penalty in IB officer Ankit Sharma murder case
Article Text:
Why the court awarded life imprisonment instead of death

Court's conviction order

NEW DELHI: A Delhi court on Friday sentenced former AAP councillor Tahir Hussain and four others to life imprisonment for the murder of Intelligence Bureau (IB) officer Ankit Sharma during the 2020 northeast Delhi riots, rejecting the prosecution's plea for the death penalty after holding that it had failed to prove the convicts were beyond the possibility of reformation.Additional Sessions Judge Praveen Singh pronounced the sentence after hearing arguments from both the prosecution and the defence on the quantum of punishment. The court said the prosecution had not established that the case met the threshold for awarding capital punishment, even though it had convicted Hussain and four others for Sharma's murder earlier this month.The judgment was delivered in the physical presence of Hussain and the other convicts amid tight security at Delhi's Karkardooma Court.While the Delhi Police had argued that the case fell within the "rarest of rare" category warranting capital punishment, the court concluded that the prosecution had not proved that the convicts were incapable of reform, a key principle laid down by the Supreme Court for awarding the death penalty.Additional Sessions Judge Praveen Singh observed that the prosecution was unable to establish that the convicts were beyond reformation, leading the court to impose life imprisonment instead.The prosecution had sought the death penalty for Hussain and the four co-convicts, arguing that the murder was brutal, deliberate and carried out without any provocation.During the sentencing hearing, Special Public Prosecutor Madhukar Pandey described the crime as "anti-social and abhorrent" and argued that it qualified as one of the "rarest of rare" cases.Pandey told the court that Sharma was subjected to a cold-blooded and savage attack with a heavy cutting weapon and that the killing could not be viewed in isolation because it occurred during the northeast Delhi riots in which 53 people lost their lives.According to the prosecution, Sharma sustained 51 injuries, seven of which were independently sufficient to cause death.The prosecution further submitted that the convicts acted without provocation and displayed complete disregard for the consequences of their actions.Earlier, Pandey had argued that the accused had fallen to the "level of being animals" while assaulting Sharma and said:"Those who are asking for mercy today should have shown mercy themselves. No mercy was shown from anyone's side. No one even took Ankit to the hospital. They are asking for mercy after committing such a brutal murder."The prosecution also argued that Hussain, being an elected municipal councillor at the time, had a greater responsibility to protect citizens instead of becoming part of the unlawful assembly.The defence, however, urged the court to show leniency, arguing that not every murder warranted capital punishment and that aggravating and mitigating circumstances must both be considered.Senior advocate Rajiv Mohan, appearing for Hussain, argued that six of the eleven accused in the case had already been acquitted and that the prosecution had failed to establish any conspiracy during the trial.The defence maintained that Hussain's conviction rested on his membership of an unlawful assembly and common intention rather than evidence showing he personally inflicted fatal injuries on Sharma.The counsel further argued that there had been no preparation or conspiracy, that Sharma had been attacked by a large crowd during widespread rioting and that Hussain's conduct during custody had remained satisfactory.Advocate Tara Narula also urged the court to consider Hussain's family circumstances, submitting that he had three children, an elderly father and that his wife was a homemaker dependent on rental income.Counsel representing the other convicts similarly pleaded for leniency, citing their family responsibilities and arguing that both communities had been involved in the violence.The court, however, rejected several of the defence's contentions before pronouncing the sentence.On July 13, the court convicted Hussain and four others for Sharma's murder.In its conviction order, the court held that Hussain was a member of a heavily armed mob that had assembled with animus against Hindus to commit rioting, arson and looting before murdering Sharma in what it described as a "savage and relentless assault."The court further held that the prosecution had proved members of the unlawful assembly knew that pursuing their common object could result in death.Ankit Sharma, an Intelligence Bureau officer, was killed during the northeast Delhi riots in February 2020 in the Dayalpur area. His mutilated body was later recovered from a drain.Hussain was convicted under Sections 302 (murder), 365 (kidnapping or abducting with intent secretly and wrongfully to confine a person), 147 (rioting), 148 (rioting armed with a deadly weapon), 153A (promoting enmity) and 188 (disobedience to an order duly promulgated by a public servant) of the Indian Penal Code, read with Section 149 relating to unlawful assembly.With Friday's sentencing order, Hussain and the four co-convicts will serve life imprisonment, while the court's decision underscores that despite the brutality of the crime, the legal threshold required for imposing the death penalty was not met because the prosecution failed to prove they were beyond the possibility of reformation.
Article Summary: A Delhi court sentenced former AAP councillor Tahir Hussain and four others to life imprisonment for the murder of Intelligence Bureau (IB) officer Ankit Sharma during the 2020 northeast Delhi riots. The court rejected the prosecution's plea for the death penalty after holding that it had failed to prove the convicts were beyond the possibility of reformation.

NEW DELHI: Exiled Bangladeshi writer and activist Taslima Nasreen returned to Kolkata on Friday, marking her first public visit to the city in nearly two decades after being forced to leave amid protests over her memoir "Dwikhandito".Describing her return as an emotional homecoming, Nasreen said coming back to Kolkata felt like returning to “my own country”.According to news agency PTI, Nasreen is scheduled to attend a programme in the city on August 1. The event is also expected to be attended by West Bengal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari and noted author Shirshendu Mukhopadhyay.This is Nasreen's first public appearance in Kolkata since 2007, when widespread protests over her memoir compelled her to leave the city, which had been her home after she fled Bangladesh in the 1990s.Her memoir "Dwikhandito" (Split in Two) was banned by the then Left Front government in West Bengal in 2003 for allegedly hurting the religious sentiments of the Muslim community.
Article Summary: Exiled Bangladeshi writer and activist Taslima Nasreen returned to Kolkata on Friday. It is her first public visit to the city in nearly two decades after being forced to leave amid protests over her memoir. Nasreen is scheduled to attend a programme in the city on August 1.

Article Title: 'Head of family PM Modi listens': BJP's Raghav Chadha hails 'historic' anti-paper leak Bill
Article Text:
BJP MP Raghav Chadha (ANI photo)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Poll Vote & Share your view Do you think stricter anti-paper leak laws will improve exam fairness? Yes, they will help No, more changes are needed 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

NEW DELHI: AAP turncoat and BJP MP Raghav Chadha on Thursday broke his prolonged silence on the paper leak issue, speaking for the first time from the ruling side in Rajya Sabha. As BJP pushed the anti-paper leak Bill in the Parliament, Chadha said he did not want headlines but spoke "wholeheartedly in support of the students of India," adding that "PM Modi heard it just like the head of a family listens. "Chadha stressed that the paper leak crisis could only be resolved through an "institutional solution" and not through "media sound-bytes", which he claimed was the approach adopted by the PM Modi-led government.BJP leader said, "I don't want headline, but an outcome."Addressing NEET aspirants, he said, "Your anger is justified. Your pain is real. And your concerns about the examination system are genuine."He further said that when students raised their voices in protest, the Prime Minister listened and acted as a "guardian" to address their concerns."Students demanded, the government acted. Historic decisions taken. System changed," Chadha said.He also said that the government "heard and delivered."Highlighting the impact of paper leaks on students, he added, "Because a paper leak does not merely compromise an examination. It can wipe out years of preparation in a single moment."He further said, "Every student deserves an examination system where hard work and merit, not a leaked paper, decide the result."Months ago, Chadha led a rebel exodus from Arvind Kejriwal-founded AAP, with seven Rajya Sabha members from the party breaking away and merging their faction with the ruling BJP.However, the Bill came under sharp criticism from the Opposition in the Rajya Sabha. Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge led the attack after Union minister Jitendra Singh tabled the Bill in the Upper House.Parliament Thursday approved the Public Examination (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026, introducing stricter penalties for paper leaks and exam-related malpractices. The government said the legislation addresses one of the biggest concerns affecting students and called for cooperation from all stakeholders to tackle the issue.The Bill was passed by a voice vote in the Rajya Sabha amid an opposition walkout, a day after it cleared the Lok Sabha.Under the amended law, individuals found guilty of paper leaks or other unfair means in public examinations will face a minimum prison term of five years, extendable to 10 years, along with a fine of up to Rs 50 lakh.For organised exam-related crimes, the Bill prescribes a minimum jail term of seven years and a fine of up to Rs 10 crore.The legislation also empowers state governments and Union Territory administrations to designate Courts of Session as special fast-track courts to try offences under the Act. These courts will conduct day-to-day proceedings and complete trials within three months of the filing of the chargesheet.The Bill further authorises the central government to constitute a special task force to investigate offences under the Act whenever necessary.
Article Summary: BJP leader said, "I don't want headline, but an outcome" Chadha led a rebel exodus from Arvind Kejriwal-founded AAP, with seven Rajya Sabha members from the party breaking away and merging their faction with the ruling BJP.

Article Title: Russia's overnight ballistic missile and drone attack on Ukraine capital Kyiv kills 9
Article Text:
Fire breaks out at Moscow's St Basil's Cathedral

At least nine people were killed and twenty-eight others were injured after Russia launched a barrage of ballistic missiles and drones targeting Ukraine's capital Kyiv overnight into Saturday. The attack damaged residential buildings, sparked multiple fires across the city and left people trapped under debris, officials said.Kyiv mayor Vitalii Klitschko had earlier said a five-storey residential building in the Solomianskyi district was struck by falling debris, causing severe damage and trapping residents inside."The first and second floors of the damaged residential building had partially collapsed," Klitschko said in a post on Telegram, adding that a fire had also broken out in the courtyard.Klitschko had said at least three people had been killed in the Russian missile attack and confirmed that several people remained trapped in the partially collapsed building. He added that five people had been hospitalised following the strikes.People were also believed to be trapped in another residential building in the Shevchenkivskyi district after the first and second floors partially collapsed, Klitschko said.Additionally, seven people were killed and 14 others injured in Kyiv's Darnytskyi district after the attack sparked fires and damaged homes, vehicles, an administrative building and other non-residential structures, emergency services told news agency AP.According to Reuters witnesses, more than a dozen explosions reverberated across the Ukrainian capital during the attack. This comes as Russia stepped up strikes on Kyiv in recent months, while Ukraine continues to face a shortage of air defence systems capable of intercepting ballistic missiles, which travel several times faster than the speed of sound.The latest bombardment came just two days after another large-scale Russian ballistic missile and drone attack across Ukraine killed 10 civilians and wounded more than 50 others. During that attack, a Russian missile also briefly entered Polish airspace.As Russian aerial attacks intensified, Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskyy reiterated Kyiv's demand for additional Patriot air defence systems from the United States and its Western allies."The Russian air strikes on our country continue and air defense, specifically interceptors for Patriot systems against ballistic missiles, remains a top priority," Zelenskyy said in a post on Telegram on Friday.The Ukrainian president also said he had spoken with US vice president JD Vance after his meeting earlier this week in Washington with president Donald Trump.The renewed appeal comes amid uncertainty over future US military support. At the Nato summit in Ankara in July, president Trump said the United States would grant Ukraine a licence to manufacture Patriot systems. However, during a Cabinet meeting at the presidential retreat at Camp David on Friday, Trump indicated that no final decision had yet been taken on the proposal.Meanwhile, a fire broke out at St Basil's Cathedral on Moscow's Red Square early Saturday before being brought under control, according to Russia's state-run TASS news agency.TASS, citing operational services, said the blaze started in the director's office on the first floor."On the first floor, in the director's office, personal belongings and furniture caught fire. The area of the fire was around 10 sq. metres," a source told the agency, as reported by Kyiv Post.The cause of the fire was not immediately known. No injuries were reported. Around 10 fire engines were deployed to the site before operational services confirmed that the fire had been extinguished, TASS said.
Article Summary: Russia launches barrage of ballistic missiles and drones targeting Ukraine's capital Kyiv. Attack damages residential buildings, sparks multiple fires and leaves people trapped under debris. Ukrainian president reiterates demand for additional Patriot air defence systems from the United States. Fire breaks out at Moscow's St Basil's Cathedral.

Article Title: ‘Dhurandhar’ gangster’s brother shot in Karachi
Article Text:
Personal enmity or gang war? Probe on into hit on Zubair Baloch

Zubair Baloch — the brother of jailed Pakistan gangster Uzair Baloch, whose ruthless ascent was dramatised in the movie ‘Dhurandhar’ — is learned to be critically wounded following a targeted drive-by shooting in Karachi’s Lyari neighbourhood on Thursday evening, reports .The 40-year-old was sitting outside his Singu Lane home when two masked assailants on a motorcycle opened fire, striking him in the chest and abdomen.Zubair was rushed to Civil Hospital Karachi for emergency surgery. Two bystanders were also injured in the crossfire, with one reported to be in serious condition.According to Pakistan police, the attackers fled after a nearby shopkeeper returned fire. CCTV footage from the spot, which surfaced on Telegram channels, showed chaos on the street as the gunmen escaped.Police told the local press they were probing angles of personal enmity and the potential resurgence of long-standing gang wars.Zubair, arrested in multiple criminal cases in 2012, was released from prison last year, while his brother Uzair remains in jail serving a 12-year sentence handed down by a military court.Uzair and several accomplices were indicted for a 2012 armed attack on law enforcement officers under Kalakot police station’s jurisdiction.In April 2020, Uzair Baloch received a 12-year prison sentence for espionage.For decades, the historic Karachi neighbourhood of Lyari served as the epicentre of a gang war and a hub of organised crime. The turmoil traces back to early turf battles over drug trade routes and extortion rackets, which eventually expanded into a high-stakes proxy war involving major political factions.Notorious figures such as Sardar Abdul Rehman Baloch aka Rehman Dakait and his fierce rival Arshad Pappu turned narrow alleyways into battlegrounds, leveraging strategic political patronage through outfits like Peoples’ Aman Committee to insulate their syndicates from police oversight. Following Rehman Dakait’s death in a 2009 police encounter, his cousin Uzair Baloch stepped in to control the dominant faction.
Article Summary: Zubair Baloch, 40, was shot in the chest and abdomen on Thursday evening. He was sitting outside his home when two masked assailants opened fire. Two bystanders were also injured in the crossfire, with one reported to be in serious condition. Police are probing angles of personal enmity and the potential resurgence of gang wars.

Article Title: 'Sorry to entire nation, I am just 15': Noida resident who 'abused' PM Modi in video apologises
Article Text:
A Noida woman accused of abusing Prime Minister Modi posted an apology video claiming she is fifteen years old.





NEW DELHI: A day after Delhi Police began examining the Zero FIR against her, Ruchika Singh , the Noida resident accused of using abusive language against Prime Minister Narendra Modi during the CJP-led Jantar Mantar protest, posted a video apologising with folded hands and her head bowed.In the video, she claimed she is 15 years old and said was "influenced" by fellow protesters.She said, "I went to visit CP with my friend. There was a protest going on, and many groups had gathered there. People were saying all sorts of things, including filthy abuses against the Prime Minister. I got influenced because they told me to say something too. I was impressed and ended up saying a lot of things. I'm just 15 years old."Also read: 'Abusing not a crime': CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke slams FIR against Noida woman She further said, "What I did is unforgivable. I said something very vulgar. But this is my first and last mistake. I will never do something like that again. I never posted that video. I want to say sorry to the entire nation. I can't even look up. Please forgive me. Please."The claim sits at odds with details gathered by police and neighbours over the past week.SHO Amit Khare of the Expressway police station, where the original Zero FIR was registered on a complaint by Ghaziabad lawyer Smriti Singh, had said Ruchika resides with her family in Faridabad and owns a flat — bought in January — at Lotus Zing society in Sector 150, Noida.Mehtab Singh, a security guard at the society, told she has lived there for several years with her mother and worked regularly until she went missing after the Jantar Mantar incident.The Zero FIR, filed under BNS Sections 352 (intentional insult to provoke breach of peace), 353(1) (public mischief) and 356(1) (defamation), was transferred from Noida to Delhi's Special Cell on Friday, since the alleged offence occurred within the capital's jurisdiction.It runs alongside a separate FIR Delhi Police had already registered over the circulation of the derogatory content, with notices issued to X seeking its removal.Also read: Social media influencer in soup over RAF personal video during CJP protest, apologises The episode has drawn PM Modi's own intervention. In an Instagram video Friday, he said the abuse — directed at him and, he said, his late mother was "a cultural shock."However, PM Modi urged restraint and appealed against punitive action."These young people should be embraced, not punished," he said, arguing that court cases and criminal proceedings would not address the larger social problem reflected in the incident.CJP spokesperson Saurav Das and founder Abhijeet Dipke have separately accused police of selective action, arguing profanity should draw civil defamation suits, not criminal cases, and pointing to alleged unpunished remarks by BJP leaders and IT-cell handles.
Article Summary: Ruchika Singh is accused of using abusive language against Prime Minister Narendra Modi during the CJP-led Jantar Mantar protest. She posted a video apologising with folded hands and her head bowed. She claimed she is 15 years old and said was "influenced" by fellow protesters.

Article Title: Reeling from powerful earthquake that killed 34, Japan hit with 5.7 magnitude quake 5 days later
Article Text:
5.7-magnitude quake hits Northern Japan days after powerful tremor

A 5.7-magnitude earthquake jolted Japan's northern Hokkaido region on Saturday, just days after a powerful 7.1 magnitude earthquake struck southwestern Japan.The 7.1-magnitude quake caused widespread destruction, triggering an explosion at a shopping mall, toppling a factory chimney and flattening homes in the city of Yatsushiro, while also leaving roads cracked and buildings damaged. Article Title: Kerala rain havoc: 2 dead, several feared trapped as landslides, floods batter state
Article Text:
Incessant heavy rainfall triggered landslides and flash floods across central Kerala on Saturday

More people feared trapped

Landslides disrupt highways

Flood situation worsens

IMD issues red alert





THIRUVANANTHAPURAM: Incessant heavy rainfall triggered landslides, flash floods and widespread disruption across central Kerala on Saturday.The incident has left at least two people dead, several others feared trapped under debris, and prompted large-scale rescue operations in multiple districts, news agency ANI reported.The worst-hit district was Idukki, where landslides claimed two lives in separate incidents.At Adoormala, a landslide buried a house, killing Sumathi.Her husband Ravi and their son were rescued by neighbours and admitted to a hospital in Thodupuzha with injuries.Officials said the family’s house was completely destroyed, news agency PTI reported.In Vagamon, another landslide struck a house, killing Prabhakaran Nair, a native of Vaikom.Rescue teams were continuing operations to recover his body.Authorities said search operations involving the National Disaster Response Force (NDRF), Fire and Rescue Services, police and revenue officials were underway in the affected areas.Rescue teams were also searching for people feared trapped under debris in Kottayam district after a landslide buried a house at Payyanithottam in Poonjar.Heavy rain caused widespread flooding in Erattupetta, Kanjirappally, Koottickal and Erumeli, inundating residential areas and disrupting road connectivity.Rescue personnel, assisted by local residents, evacuated families stranded on the upper floors of their homes, while rising water levels forced authorities to suspend vehicular movement in several areas.Floodwaters also submerged the Koottickal and Mundakkayam causeways after the Manimala and Pullakayar rivers overflowed.The continuing downpour triggered multiple landslides across Idukki, severely affecting transport.A major landslide near Machiplavu in Adimali on the Kochi-Dhanushkodi National Highway brought traffic to a standstill after a car and a Taurus lorry were caught in the debris.The Kattappana-Vazhavara Road was blocked by another landslide, while overflowing water from the Chottupara stream caused waterlogging on National Highway 183 at Vandiperiyar.Vehicular movement was also disrupted at Nellimala.At Upputhara, a parked police jeep was damaged after a landslide.Authorities also opened the shutters of several minor dams in Idukki following the continuous rainfall.The overflowing Pullakayar River submerged the Kokkayar low-level crossing, inundating around six houses. The affected families were shifted to safer locations.Fresh landslides were also reported from hilly areas of Pathanamthitta district.Ranni MLA Pazhakulam Madhu said river levels had reached dangerous levels in Ranni and surrounding areas, with floodwaters entering several houses and commercial establishments.The India Meteorological Department (IMD) forecast continued heavy rainfall across Kerala and issued a red alert for Pathanamthitta, Kottayam, Idukki, Malappuram, Kozhikode, Wayanad, Kannur and Kasaragod districts, warning of very heavy rainfall.An orange alert has been issued for Ernakulam, Thrissur and Palakkad districts.District administrations declared holidays for schools in several districts, while authorities advised people living in landslide- and flood-prone areas to remain alert as rescue and relief operations continued.(With agency inputs)
Article Summary: Incessant heavy rainfall triggered landslides, flash floods and widespread disruption across central Kerala on Saturday. The incident has left at least two people dead, several others feared trapped under debris, and prompted large- scale rescue operations. The worst-hit district was Idukki, where landslides claimed two lives in separate incidents.

Article Title: Singapore student Siti Aishah Siregar left home saying she was going to college; hours later her family found her passport missing and a Cambodia flight ticket in her email
Article Text:
S'pore NYP student said she was going to school, vanished, family found Cambodia flight ticket in email

Singapore student Siti Aishah Siregar left home saying she was going to college; hours later her family found her passport missing and a Cambodia flight ticket in her email.Singapore police confirmed that the 20-year-old had already left the country on an outbound flight, prompting an urgent search to track her down in Phnom Penh.According to the teenager's eldest brother, Syafiq Siregar, who spoke to news outlet Berita Mediacorp, Aishah informed her mother at around 11am on 28 July that she was travelling to Nanyang Polytechnic as usual.Concerns grew later that afternoon when family members arrived at the college campus at about 5pm to pick her up. They discovered that her mobile phone was completely unreachable and her WhatsApp account had been deactivated.Upon returning home, the family noticed that Aishah's passport was missing from the house. After logging into her email account, they uncovered a flight ticket booking confirmation bound for Phnom Penh, Cambodia.Her father, Sahat Siregar, issued an emotional appeal on Facebook on 30 July, begging authorities in both Singapore and Cambodia for immediate assistance to locate his daughter.He wrote that his daughter is believed to be in Phnom Penh and appealed directly to officials and members of the public to "bring Aishah back home".In his post, he asked authorities to "please help us find my daughter as soon as possible".The family confirmed they have lodged a formal police report in Singapore and are working closely with law enforcement. Expressing the family's growing anxiety, the father highlighted that every moment counts."We are afraid that every hour we lose could make it harder to bring her home safely," he wrote in the post, adding, "As a father, I am begging for your help. I just want my daughter to come home safe."In his appeal, Sahat thanked those who had assisted the family and requested that people share his message widely across social media, noting that "someone may have seen something or know something that could help"."If you have any information, no matter how small, please contact me or the Singapore police immediately," he wrote. "Please keep my daughter in your prayers. Please help bring my daughter home safely."
Article Summary: Singapore student Siti Aishah Siregar left home saying she was going to college. Her family found her passport missing and a Cambodia flight ticket in her email. Singapore police confirmed that the 20-year-old had already left the country on an outbound flight.

Article Title: US, Israel weigh bombarding Iran's energy infrastructure through the weekend: Report
Article Text:
US, Israel eye weekend bombing campaign on Iran's energy sites

The United States and Israel are planning a potential bombing campaign targeting Iran's energy infrastructure, with strikes possibly taking place over the weekend, CBS News reported on Friday, citing sources.However, US president Donald Trump has not yet given final approval for the operation.According to multiple US sources, officials have discussed wrapping up the operation before financial markets open on Monday amid concerns over the potential impact of the strikes on the US and global economy.However, no firm timeline has been finalised.The sources added that Israeli officials have been informed of the plans and are coordinating closely with the United States.A joint operation would mark Israel's return to active military operations after it paused its campaign during the US-brokered truce.Iran, meanwhile, has not launched attacks against Israel since the memorandum of understanding collapsed and the United States resumed combat operations in early July."Israel is unaware of a decision to restart full military operations, nor has been requested of Israel to join any military actions against Iran," an Israeli official was quoted as saying by CBS News.The development comes as Trump warned on Friday that Iran could be hit "very hard.""We'll be hitting him very hard and, you know, at some point they're going to say, 'We just can't take it anymore'," the US president said.The Wall Street Journal also reported that Trump had ordered preparations for a fresh military offensive aimed at pressuring Tehran into surrender, with the operation potentially beginning as early as this weekend.More than five months after the conflict began on February 28, when the United States and Israel launched strikes on Iran, the fighting shows no sign of easing, with both sides continuing to exchange attacks.Throughout the conflict, Trump has repeatedly threatened to target Iran's critical infrastructure. Last week, he warned that the United States would destroy a bridge or power plant each time commercial shipping in the strategically important Strait of Hormuz came under attack.The latest report also comes days after Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu met Trump and US defence secretary Pete Hegseth in Washington.
Article Summary: US, Israel eye weekend bombing campaign on Iran's energy sites, sources say. US president Donald Trump has not yet given final approval for the operation. Israeli officials have been informed of the plans and are coordinating closely with the United States. A joint operation would mark Israel's return to active military operations.

Article Title: Uttarakhand CM Dhami hears public grievances, orders swift redressal
Article Text:
Uttarakhand CM Dhami hears public grievances, orders swift redressal





DEHRADUN: Uttarakhand chief minister Pushkar Singh Dhami on Friday met people from different parts of the state at the Mukhya Sevak Sadan, located at the Chief Minister's Camp Office, and listened to their grievances. He directed concerned officials to ensure prompt and effective resolution of public issues.The chief minister also instructed officials from the chief minister's office, along with the Garhwal Commissioner and Inspector General (IG) of Garhwal, to accord top priority to the disposal of public complaints.He emphasised that there should be no unnecessary delay in resolving grievances and that timely relief must be provided to the affected citizens.On the occasion, Kedarnath MLA Asha Nautiyal met the chief minister along with a delegation and expressed gratitude to him for the successful and smooth conduct of this year's Kedarnath Yatra and the Char Dham Yatra so far.Nautiyal said that the state government's continuous monitoring and efficient management of the pilgrimage had helped ensure better facilities and a hassle-free experience for devotees.MLA Bhupal Ram Tamta also met the chief minister with a delegation and thanked the state government for prioritising local interests while addressing key issues related to the state's alpine meadows (Bugyals).The delegation said that Uttarakhand's Bugyals are an integral part of the state's natural and cultural heritage, with the livelihoods of many local residents and tourism activities closely linked to them. They stated that under the leadership of chief minister Pushkar Singh Dhami, the state government has been consistently working to strike a balance between environmental conservation and the promotion of local employment, tourism, and livelihoods.The public representatives appreciated the government's efforts to promote development while taking into account the unique geographical and local conditions of the hill regions. They expressed confidence that better coordination between local interests, environmental conservation, and tourism development would create new employment opportunities in the mountainous areas and further strengthen the local economy.CM Dhami said that the state government's priority is the timely resolution of public grievances and the balanced development of every region of the state. He directed officials to address public issues with sensitivity, efficiency, and a sense of urgency.
Article Summary: Uttarakhand chief minister Pushkar Singh Dhami on Friday met people from different parts of the state. He directed concerned officials to ensure prompt and effective resolution of public issues. Kedarnath MLA Asha Nautiyal met the chief minister along with a delegation and expressed gratitude to him for the successful and smooth conduct of this year's Yatra.

Article Title: Spain says most migrants return to Morocco after border rush kills 57
Article Text:
As thousands gathered near the border, Moroccan security forces used batons and tear gas to push back crowds

Spain said on Friday that it had regained control of a massive migrant surge into its North African enclave of Ceuta, with most of the more than 50,000 people who crossed the border by land and sea voluntarily returning to Morocco. The unprecedented influx left dozens dead and triggered political tensions across Europe.Spanish authorities said 57 bodies had been recovered on the Spanish side of the border. Officials warned that the death toll could be higher as there may have been additional casualties on the Moroccan side. According to the government, some migrants drowned while others were crushed as they attempted to climb the breakwater supporting the border fence.Spain's interior ministry said around 50,000 migrants entered Ceuta between Thursday and Friday, with about 48,300 having already returned to Morocco by Friday evening. Ceuta regional president Juan Jesus Vivas, however, estimated that the total number of crossings could have reached 60,000 over the two days.As thousands gathered near the border, Moroccan security forces used batons and tear gas to push back crowds and prevent more people from entering the Spanish territory.Reuters reporters at the scene also saw riot police firing tear gas, while water cannon vehicles were deployed to disperse migrants. Burnt remains of a bus and seven cars were visible following clashes.On the Spanish side, military vehicles were positioned along sections of the border as hundreds of migrants remained stranded on the Moroccan side. Several hundred people later crossed back through official checkpoints and openings in the fence, with many saying they were unable to find food or shelter in Ceuta. "I'm going back," one migrant told news agency Reuters.Spanish prime minister Pedro Sanchez travelled to Ceuta on Friday, where he faced protests and jeers from demonstrators. He described the mass border crossing as "a violation of Spain's territorial sovereignty" and said authorities were accelerating the return of those who had entered illegally with Morocco's full cooperation.The incident also exposed divisions within Europe over migration policy. Italy announced it was temporarily suspending the European Union's Schengen border-free travel arrangements with Spain, a decision that would affect air and sea travel between the two countries. Madrid criticised the move, saying it breached European Union treaties.Ceuta and Melilla, Spain's two autonomous enclaves in North Africa, form the European Union's only land borders with Africa. While both regularly witness attempts by migrants to enter Europe, Spanish authorities described the latest influx as unprecedented.Several right-wing political parties across Europe blamed the crisis on Spain's migration policies, including this year's amnesty for hundreds of thousands of undocumented migrants. Spain also summoned the Italian ambassador after Italian Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani claimed the amnesty had "encouraged human trafficking".US President Donald Trump also weighed in on the crisis, describing the situation at Ceuta as an invasion.The crossings "look like an invasion", Trump said, adding, "That same thing's going to happen to us if the Republicans don't get elected, except worse," referring to the upcoming US midterm elections.The US state department also criticised Spain's handling of migration, saying the incident was "the direct result of the Spanish Government's deliberate efforts to enable and facilitate mass illegal migration into Europe." It added, "We are considering actions to defend Americans at home and abroad from this threat and stand ready to assist other European allies considering similar option."Meanwhile, France said it would significantly strengthen security along its border with Spain.French interior minister Laurent Nunez announced that the police presence would be increased fivefold by Saturday, alongside enhanced aerial surveillance and additional patrols on trains.Spain's Guardia Civil police association AUGC also criticised the handling of the situation, saying there had been too few officers deployed at the border fence during the surge, leaving security forces unable to stop the mass crossings.
Article Summary: Spain says it has regained control of a massive migrant surge into its North African enclave of Ceuta. Most of the more than 50,000 people who crossed the border by land and sea voluntarily returned to Morocco. The unprecedented influx left dozens dead and triggered political tensions across Europe.

Article Title: 4.7-magnitude earthquake hits Italy; buildings damaged, four injured
Article Text:
4.7-magnitude earthquake strikes Italy, injures four (Reuters image)

A 4.7-magnitude earthquake struck the volcanic Campi Flegrei (Phlegraean Fields) area near the southern Italian city of Naples on Friday, injuring four people, damaging buildings and churches. It also triggered power outages that disrupted train and metro services.The earthquake struck at 7.46 pm (local time), with its epicentre in the Campi Flegrei volcanic area west of Naples at a depth of about 3 km (2 miles), according to Italy's National Institute of Geophysics and Volcanology.The Italian fire service said minor damage was reported to buildings in and around Naples, but added that emergency crews had not received any immediate requests for rescue or assistance, as cited by Reuters.As a precaution, local authorities suspended rail and metro services while inspections were carried out.Italian media described the tremor as one of the strongest ever recorded in the Campi Flegrei area, prompting residents in several neighbourhoods to rush onto the streets as the ground shook.Campi Flegrei, a densely populated volcanic caldera that spans much of western Naples, has witnessed increasingly frequent seismic activity in recent years, prompting Italian authorities to intensify monitoring of the area.While low-intensity tremors are common in the region, stronger earthquakes have revived concerns over a repeat of the seismic crisis of the early 1980s, which caused widespread disruption and forced thousands of residents to evacuate their homes.Italy is prone to earthquakes due to its geological setting. In 2016, a series of powerful quakes struck central Italy, devastating parts of the Lazio, Umbria and Marche regions and killing around 300 people.The country's deadliest earthquake in recent decades was the 6.9-magnitude Irpinia quake in southern Italy in November 1980, which claimed about 2,700 lives and devastated hundreds of towns.
Article Summary: 4.7-magnitude earthquake strikes Italy, injures four people. Epicentre in Campi Flegrei volcanic area west of Naples at a depth of about 3 km. Italian media described tremor as one of the strongest ever recorded.

Article Title: US Marine F-35 fighter jet crashes in San Diego, pilot ejects safely
Article Text:
Military officials said the cause of the crash is being investigated.

A US Marine Corps F-35 fighter jet crashed near Marine Corps Air Station (MCAS) Miramar in San Diego on Friday, with the pilot ejecting safely before the aircraft burst into flames and sparked a brush fire, military officials said.The fighter aircraft, attached to the 3rd Marine Aircraft Wing and Marine Aircraft Group 11, went down at around 10 am local time near the air station. The Marine Corps described the incident as an "aircraft mishap".First Lieutenant Blake Starbuck told Fox News that the crash was a "Class A mishap involving a Marine Corps F-35B in the vicinity of MCAS Miramar".Lieutenant Starbuck confirmed that the pilot successfully ejected and was safely recovered after the aircraft came down. Military officials said the cause of the crash is being investigated.Starbuck said he could not immediately confirm the purpose of the flight, including whether the aircraft had been taking off, landing or carrying out a training mission.He also said there was no immediate information about any injuries or fatalities linked to the crash.Television footage from SkyRanger 7 showed the wreckage split into two large sections in the middle of a burnt field roughly the size of a football pitch.Large flames and thick black smoke rose from the crash site, which was located north of State Route 52, making the fire visible to motorists on the nearby highway. The San Diego Fire-Rescue Department said it had joined efforts to contain the brush fire triggered by the crash.However, officials said the military remains in charge of the crash site and will lead the investigation into the incident.
Article Summary: US Marine Corps F-35 fighter jet crashed near Marine Corps Air Station (MCAS) Miramar in San Diego on Friday. Pilot ejected safely before the aircraft burst into flames and sparked a brush fire. Military officials said the cause of the crash is being investigated.

Article Title: This 44-year-old Swedish man survived being buried beneath a metre of snow for nearly two months against all odds
Article Text:
Image: Left/The Telegraph/Right/The Guardian

Snowmobilers uncovered the buried car after noticing something unusual beneath the snow

Doctors believed melted snow and an extremely slow metabolism helped keep him alive

The case challenged assumptions about the limits of human survival

One of the most remarkable modern survival stories

In December 2011, a 44-year-old Swedish man named Peter Skyllberg disappeared while driving through the country's frozen north. Weeks passed with no sign of him as winter temperatures plunged well below freezing. Then, in February 2012, a group of snowmobilers spotted what looked like the roof of a car protruding from a snowdrift. Digging through nearly a metre of snow, they made an astonishing discovery: inside sat the missing driver, alive but severely weakened after spending almost two months trapped inside the snow-covered vehicle with little or no food. His extraordinary survival stunned doctors and scientists alike, raising questions about how the human body can endure prolonged starvation and extreme cold under exceptional circumstances. The case remains one of the most remarkable survival stories on record, highlighting the body's extraordinary ability to adapt under rare conditions while continuing to inform medical understanding of hypothermia, starvation and human resilience.Peter Skyllberg, a 44-year-old Swedish man, had apparently become stranded on a remote road after his vehicle was immobilised by heavy snowfall during late December.As reported by the BBC, over the following weeks, repeated snowstorms gradually buried the car beneath roughly one metre of snow, leaving only a small portion visible above the surface. On 17 February 2012, passing snowmobilers noticed the unusual shape beneath the snow and stopped to investigate. After digging into the drift, they found the driver sitting inside the vehicle, barely able to move or speak but still conscious. Emergency responders transported him by helicopter to hospital, where doctors began treating him for severe dehydration, malnutrition and hypothermia.Medical specialists estimated that the man had survived for close to two months with virtually no food. According to doctors treating him, he is believed to have survived primarily by melting and drinking snow, preventing fatal dehydration while his body relied on stored fat reserves for energy. Physicians also suggested that prolonged exposure to cold may have pushed his body into an extreme energy-conservation state, dramatically slowing metabolism and reducing calorie requirements.Rather than freezing, the man may have benefited from the very snow that trapped him. The thick blanket of snow covering the vehicle acted as a natural insulating layer, shielding the interior from the harshest outdoor temperatures and helping maintain a more stable environment than the open air outside.Although humans can survive for weeks without food under certain conditions, surviving for nearly two months in such an isolated environment is exceptionally rare.Doctors involved in the case described the survival as extraordinary, noting that each situation depends on numerous factors, including hydration, body fat, physical activity, environmental conditions and underlying health.The Swedish case also highlighted the protective role snow can sometimes play. While heavy snowfall often creates life-threatening situations, deep snow can also trap pockets of relatively warmer air, reducing heat loss in much the same way that insulated shelters or snow caves protect mountaineers during winter storms.The man's identity was never widely publicised, and after receiving medical treatment he gradually recovered from the ordeal.His case remains one of the most extraordinary documented examples of human endurance in modern times. Rather than surviving through extraordinary supplies or specialised equipment, he endured weeks of isolation using little more than melted snow while remaining inside a vehicle buried beneath winter drifts.The incident continues to fascinate survival experts and physicians because it demonstrates how, under exceptional circumstances, the human body can adapt far beyond what most people would consider possible. It also serves as a reminder of both the dangers of remote winter travel and the remarkable resilience that can emerge when survival depends on conserving every possible ounce of energy.
Article Summary: Peter Skyllberg, a 44-year-old Swedish man, had apparently become stranded on a remote road after his vehicle was immobilised by heavy snowfall. Snowmobilers uncovered the buried car after noticing something unusual beneath the snow. Doctors believed melted snow and an extremely slow metabolism helped keep him alive. The case challenged assumptions about the limits of human survival.
